newsitem.title: FRANCE: French jobless seen rising in January.
newsitem.headline: French jobless seen rising in January.

text.p: The old adage of "lies, damn lies and statistics" will be foremost in some experts minds when France publishes its first monthly unemployment statistics for 1997 on Friday.
Economists say a surprise drop in unemployment in December was largely due to a dampening effect of changes in procedures for registering as unemployed and that the underlying trend is still rising.

They expect the labour ministry to report an increase in the number of jobless in January and contend that if their predictions are once again faulted by the figures, it will be due to a repeat of the same phenomenon.
While few of them are happy with making precise predictions, the general view is that the number out of work could have risen by anything from 5,000 to 20,000 following a December fall of 29,000.

At issue is a change introduced late last year under which people now register as unemployed with the agency responsible for distributing unemployment benefit, UNEDIC, rather than the agency which tries to find work for the jobless, the ANPE.

Economists believe that, even if the motive was in fact to simplify registration procedures, the effect of this change is that it discourages young people joining the labour market from registering as unemployed when they have not worked before and are not therefore entitled to UNEDIC unemployment benefits.

Pierre Alain Muet, a director at the OFCE, an authoritative, independent economic think-tank, says the drop in the December figures was a "statistical miracle" and that the marked drop in youth unemployment proves the point that the procedural changes are deterring young people from registering.
The December figures showed a marked 2.1 percent drop in the number of young men out of work and a 2.6 percent drop for women aged under 25 years.
Muet says that experts in the labour ministry have come up with an as yet unpublished estimate that the changes could cut the number registering as unemployed by 100,000 in a year.
"Young people registering with the ANPE risk not registering with the Assedic (arm of the UNEDIC agency)," said Muet.
"That could amount to 100,000 a year, or a little less than 10,000 a month," he says.
His view is shared by several private bank economists.

David Naude, economist at U.S. bank JP Morgan in Paris, says unemployment could have risen by 20,000 in January and that the trend in the medium term is for France's unemployment rate, now at a record 12.7 percent -- to push up towards 13 percent.
The drop in December, he says, must be largely due to the impact of the procedural changes.
"My suspicion is that it had to have an impact. Otherwise there's no explanation," Naude said.
Deutsche bank economist Patrick Mange believes there will be a rise of 10-12,000 in unemployment in January.
He nevertheless contends that the impact of the changes in registering practice will be marginal.

Les Echos newspaper reported ANPE managing director Michel Bernard on Wednesday as saying that a survey involving 28 ANPE agencies led to the conclusion that the changes could result in a 10 percent reduction in the number of people registering as jobseekers each month.
